description: 2nd connection. 1st connection confirmed the important part (full seed+solution compile, Highest Severity 00, now recorded in docs/probes.md) but the bsh and add-a-PF checks failed on two of my own mistakes: bsh's real path is /QOpenSys/usr/bin/bsh (not /usr/bin/bsh - the 1st connection's own ls output already showed this via the symlink), and the add-a-PF test's CPYTOSTMF referenced &LIB2 for a file-type-delivered member, but file-type steps always deliver to &LIB regardless of library2. Both fixed here. Also broadens the GENERATE_SQL SYSPARMS query (0 rows under SPECIFIC_SCHEMA='QSYS2' last time, despite the query itself working - real column names confirmed) to just SPECIFIC_NAME LIKE '%GENERATE_SQL%' with no schema filter, in case it's cataloged under a different schema.

steps.label: BSHTEST
steps.cmd:
ls -la /QOpenSys/usr/bin/bsh </dev/null 2>&1
echo ---BSH-DEFAULT-PATH---
/QOpenSys/usr/bin/bsh -c 'echo $PATH' </dev/null 2>&1
echo ---BSH-MAKEI-VERSION---
/QOpenSys/usr/bin/bsh -c 'export PATH=/QOpenSys/pkgs/bin:$PATH; echo PATH=$PATH; makei --version' </dev/null 2>&1

steps.label: PFEXERCISE
steps.cmd:
rm -rf "$HOME/mkpf"
mkdir -p "$HOME/mkpf/z"
system "CPYTOSTMF FROMMBR('/QSYS.LIB/&LIB.LIB/QDDSSRC.FILE/TESTPF.MBR') TOSTMF('$HOME/mkpf/z/testpf.pf') STMFOPT(*REPLACE) STMFCCSID(1208) ENDLINFMT(*LF)" 2>&1
/QOpenSys/pkgs/bin/python3 -c "open('$HOME/mkpf/z/Rules.mk','wb').write(b'TESTPF.FILE: testpf.pf\n')"
/QOpenSys/pkgs/bin/python3 -c "open('$HOME/mkpf/z/iproj.json','wb').write(b'{\"version\":\"0.0.1\",\"objlib\":\"&LIB2\",\"curlib\":\"&LIB2\"}')"
echo ---TREE---
find "$HOME/mkpf/z" -type f </dev/null
echo ---BUILD---
/QOpenSys/pkgs/bin/bash -c 'cd "$HOME/mkpf/z" && export PATH=/QOpenSys/pkgs/bin:$PATH && /QOpenSys/pkgs/bin/makei build' </dev/null 2>&1
echo ---CLEANUP---
system "DLTF FILE(&LIB2/TESTPF)" 2>&1
rm -rf "$HOME/mkpf"

steps.sql: SELECT SPECIFIC_SCHEMA, SPECIFIC_NAME, ORDINAL_POSITION, PARAMETER_MODE, PARAMETER_NAME, DATA_TYPE, CHARACTER_MAXIMUM_LENGTH FROM QSYS2.SYSPARMS WHERE SPECIFIC_NAME LIKE '%GENERATE_SQL%' ORDER BY SPECIFIC_SCHEMA, ORDINAL_POSITION
